name: PT Kino Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Kino Indonesia — a real earnings recovery that the price already carries
frontmatter.summary: Kino's first half doubled operating profit and the balance sheet is deleveraging, but at ten times our forward earnings the market has already paid for it. The interim dividend sits inside the payout we model, but free cash flow to equity covers only part and the cash balance funds the rest: the target and rating are unchanged, HOLD.
thesis: Kino is a challenger FMCG house: beverages, personal care, food, pet food and pharmaceuticals, with a controlled owner and a public float of about one share in seven.
The 2026 half-year is an actual, not a promise, but it is now in the price: the shares trade at a forward multiple a little above the larger staples names, on earnings that still contain a one-off.

Restating D&A from the notes rather than the data pack turns EBITDA into a coherent number; on that measure FY2025 debt was three point seven times EBITDA against a four-times covenant, so the leverage test clears by a quarter of a turn and the relief the banks gave names the current ratio.
Deleveraging is the clearest company-specific fact and it is in our base case, but in an unlevered DCF it reaches the target only through the dividend, which is why it does not rescue the rating.

The sweetened-beverage excise from H2-2027 lands on more than half of sales with the rate unset; that, plus a thin float, is why the probability-weighted value after the liquidity discount sits below the price.
The dividend is covered by free cash flow to equity only in part: the balance sheet funds the rest, which is the main risk to the income case on a company that needed four covenant waivers.

catalysts.event: Record date for the FY2026 interim dividend, payable early December
Nine-month 2026 accounts — whether the second-quarter operating margin holds through the third quarter, against the profit line the dividend announcement already disclosed
FY2026 audited accounts and the FY2027 dividend proposal
Implementing regulation for the MBDK excise — the rate and the sugar threshold
First half-year of the excise regime (targeted start H2-2027)
First covenant test after the balance-sheet date, on the FY2027 accounts

blocks.text: **What this update changes.** On 5 November 2026 the board declared an FY2026 interim dividend of Rp52 a share — IDR71.7bn, record date 19 November, payment 9 December [S7, S8]. It is the first interim in the record we hold and 32.3% of the IDR222.2bn nine-month attributable profit [S0, S7, S9], part of the Rp80 a share the model carries, so the payout stays at 49.6% and the target and rating do not move [S7].

**The nine-month base.** Two reports date the profit base to 30 September and one calls it the first half [S7]; the first-half reading is impossible, so we use the nine months and cite the filing [S9]. The re-base exposed a defect the old FY2026 line carried — a full year below the nine months already earned, caused by an unsourced SG&A give-back, now removed. FY2026E carries attributable profit of IDR222.4bn, a little above the nine months [S0, S3, S9], and the tax charge lands at the year end, so the November accounts are the test [S0, S8].

**Rating HOLD, target Rp1,347, total return -9.1% against Rp1,570.** The base DCF is Rp1,529; rolled forward a year at the cost of equity Rp1,647; bear, base and bull at 25.0%, 55.0% and 20.0% weight to Rp1,683; the 20.0% illiquidity discount takes it to Rp1,347. The discount, not the operating view, turns a small fundamental premium into a negative return.

Kino is a mid-cap consumer group — beverages, personal care, food, pet food and pharmaceuticals — and a challenger in every category against Indofood, Wings, Mayora and Unilever [S3]. FY2025 was its first clean year after the FY2022 loss; the 2026 first half broke from that base and our forecast reproduces it: revenue IDR5,239.5bn, EBITDA IDR611.1bn, EPS Rp161 [S0, S3].

The variant view is narrow: the recovery is real and priced. The shares trade at 9.7x our FY2026E earnings and 5.6x EV/EBITDA, yielding 1.9% on free cash flow to equity. Our DCF value of Rp1,529 is close to the price, and the 13.5% float costs a fifth of that value to own. Three things move it: whether the first half's cost ratio holds; the pace of repayment, with interest falling from IDR129.3bn to IDR79.0bn by FY2030; and the excise from H2-2027 on beverages, 53.0% of revenue [S0, S3, S4].

Kino manufactures and sells consumer goods in five segments: beverages are 53.0% of revenue, personal care 36.7%, with food, pet food and pharmaceuticals making up the rest [S3]. The portfolio is brand-led — Ellips, Eskulin, Cap Kaki Tiga, Ristra — with production in-house; the FY2025 report gives personal-care production of 13,420 kl against installed capacity of 84,259 kl, beverages at 287,934 kl and food at 11,490,232 kg [S3].

The footprint is Indonesian with overseas entities in Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, India and Japan, selling through general and modern trade [S3]. Management guided 2026 growth in line with GDP on launches, efficiency, promotion and distribution [S3]; the first half delivered far more, so either the plan was conservative or the second half gives some back.

The founder's holding company controls 79.0% and the founder is president director [S3]: a controlled company with a small float, 4,847.0 employees and a market capitalisation of IDR2,164.7bn at Rp1,570 [S3, S0].

Indonesian consumer staples is a volume game in a young, urbanising population. Growth is a function of nominal consumption, the volume/price split and input costs — sugar, palm derivatives, wheat, packaging and the rupiah; the company points to domestic demand carrying the industry while exports slow [S3].

Our deck prices the inputs: CPO at US$1,240/t for FY2027E against a spot of US$1,180/t, with wheat, corn and soymeal following similar paths [S3]. We use CPO as a proxy for palm-derived surfactants and packaging, with a fifth of cost of goods sold exposed and four-fifths of any move passed through. The macro deck has the rupiah at Rp18,350/USD and the policy rate at 5.75%; the debt reprices and part of the input bill is imported [S3].

Indonesian FMCG has historically been a premium-multiple sector, and the past several years have been a
de-rating story rather than an earnings story. For a mid-cap challenger the base rate is not whether it will
grow but what multiple the market will still pay. We treat the multiple as a constraint, not a source.

Regulation is where the industry view becomes company-specific. The government has committed to an MBDK excise from H2-2027 and written a revenue target into the 2027 budget, but the rate and sugar threshold are unset [S4]. The target is IDR1,700.0bn of MBDK revenue in APBN 2027 [S6, S4] — of the same order as Kino's entire beverage revenue, 53.0% of IDR4,421.6bn [S3] — so the levy must be spread across a category many times Kino's size at a low rate, which rules out extracting Kino's beverage margin in year one. It has been postponed before, a sugar basis allows reformulation, and the industry will pass what it can into prices [S4, S3].

Competitive position: Kino is a challenger in every category — personal care against Unilever and Wings, beverages against Mayora, Wings and Indofood, food against local producers — with distribution density and brand breadth as its edge, not pricing power [S3]. Supplier power is moderate and rising; buyer power is high in modern trade; substitutes are a high threat in beverages; rivalry is intense and promotional, which is why selling expense runs above a third of revenue [S3].

**The restatement that matters.** The data pack's FY2025 D&A is about a quarter of the real charge: PPE depreciation IDR168.1bn [S3, F35], right-of-use IDR11.7bn and IDR16.9bn [S3, F20, F21] and amortisation IDR7.3bn [S3, F22], together IDR204.0bn; FY2024 is built the same way for IDR206.6bn [S3, S5], and both totals are DERIVED in F3 and F4. EBIT is unchanged, but EBITDA becomes IDR417.2bn at 9.4%, the lenders' measure: FY2025 debt is three point seven times EBITDA against the 4.0x limit, a quarter of a turn, not the pack's wide cushion [S3]. The waivers name the current ratio, so the LK does not prove the leverage test was untouched [S3].

**Revenue and margins.** FY2025 sales of IDR4,421.6bn grew only 1.2% on a soft first half [S3]. The 2026 first half grew more than a fifth; our 18.5% full-year growth implies H2 decelerates on a tougher base, then we fade to 8.0% because the excise lands mid-year [S0, S3, S4]. Gross margin was 43.6% and is 43.3% — the last actual repeated, not an expansion [S0, S3]. The recovery is in the cost base: selling plus administrative expense ran at IDR1,712.5bn in FY2025, while the H1 ratio was materially lower as promotion and sales-force costs lagged revenue [S3, S0]. We hold the achieved ratio, which is why EBITDA margin of 11.7% exceeds 9.4%: H1 operating profit on the restated D&A rate gives about a twelve per cent half-year EBITDA margin and implied H2 about eleven and a half, carrying the year's CPO drag [S0, S3].

**Below the operating line.** In FY2025, EBIT of IDR213.1bn less gross interest IDR129.3bn plus interest income IDR1.9bn plus other income IDR72.7bn gives pre-tax IDR158.4bn [S0, S3]. FY2026E: EBIT IDR370.1bn less interest IDR113.2bn plus income IDR1.9bn plus other IDR26.1bn gives pre-tax IDR284.9bn [S0]. We annualise the H1 other-income item in FY2026 and carry nil after, which is why FY2026 attributable profit of IDR222.4bn exceeds FY2027's IDR210.0bn even as operating profit rises [S0]. The interest line uses the paid rate, 7.2%, on opening debt, the valuation the marginal rate [S3, S0].

**The debt path.** The row carries the full-year movement from the June sheet, so year-end debt is IDR1,345.0bn and FY2027 interest IDR97.5bn [S0, S3]. From FY2027 we repay IDR-130.0bn falling to IDR-40.0bn by FY2030; FY2025's pace is not repeated because it was part-funded by a working-capital release — operating cash flow IDR632.2bn against net profit IDR125.9bn plus D&A IDR204.0bn [S3, F5, F3]. Faster repayment reaches the target only through interest, leverage and the deducted dividend [S0, S3].

**Cash flow and capex.** FY2025 operating cash flow of IDR632.2bn against net profit of IDR125.9bn is cash conversion several times earnings, explained by restated D&A and a supplier-payment release that does not repeat [S3]. We model working capital at 8.0% of sales, between the FY2025 level of IDR455.8bn and the lower June position [S0, S3], and correct the half-year stub in the valuation bridge so H2 builds to the target [S0]. Capex was IDR208.1bn in FY2025, 4.7% of sales and up sharply [S3]; we hold it near D&A while capacity absorbs growth, then lift it above D&A from FY2029 because the growth must be paid for [S3].

**Balance sheet, covenants and liquidity.** Net debt was IDR1,437.6bn at FY2025, 3.4x EBITDA, and fell again by June [S0, S3]. Covenants: current ratio 1.0x, debt/equity 2.5x, debt/EBITDA 4.0x, DSCR 1.0x, tested annually [S3]. FY2025 current assets of IDR1,580.5bn against liabilities of IDR2,375.9bn were below the current-ratio test, and waivers came from CIMB, CTBC, OCBC and BCA between 20 February and 30 March 2026 [S3]. The breach was not cured by June, so the December 2026 test rests on H2 season and a rolled waiver: a liquidity flag [S0, S3]. Leverage is not binding on our forecast — net debt/EBITDA 2.0x — but the current ratio is [S0]. Equity of IDR1,746.3bn includes a revaluation surplus, so we do not use P/B [S3].

**Capital allocation and cash cover.** The payout has been ratcheted to Rp45 a share, 50.2% of attributable profit, and the interim is the first instalment of the Rp80 total at the same 49.6% [S3, S0, S7, S8]. The honest coverage measure is FCFE, not FCFF. FCFF of IDR325.6bn is struck before the IDR113.2bn interest charge — about four-fifths after tax — and before the modelled net repayment. After both, FCFE is IDR40.5bn in FY2026E against a cash dividend of IDR62.0bn, and IDR45.4bn in FY2027E against IDR110.3bn when the declared FY2026 dividend is paid [S0]. FCFE covers neither. The shortfall comes from the balance sheet: cash falls from IDR123.8bn to IDR102.2bn and IDR37.3bn. Net debt still falls because the same flow repays debt, so no new borrowing survives on the net-debt line, but the payout is part-funded by the cash buffer on a balance sheet that needed four waivers. The dividend is a liquidity claim, not a free-cash-flow one, and that is the main risk to the HOLD income case; retained earnings of IDR634.7bn are accounting capacity, not cash [S9].

**Earnings-quality flags.** The accruals ratio is strongly negative in the good sense and receivables are not outgrowing revenue [S3]; there is no capitalised development cost of consequence, no IDX special-monitoring or notation flag, no pledge and no rights issue since listing [S2, S3], and related-party payables to PT Royal Bintang Persada were IDR7.5bn against liabilities of IDR2,722.2bn [S3]. Nothing is manipulation class; the float is a liquidity flag, not a governance one.

Kino is a consumer staples compounder, so value is cash after the reinvestment needed to keep growing: a discounted free-cash-flow model is the primary method and the only one we weight. A P/E leg would be mechanical — the engine applies any peer multiple to last-twelve-month EPS of Rp90, about half the earning power of our FY2026E Rp161 — and the dividend-yield leg capitalises the dividend at a market yield, not a required return. Both stay visible as cross-checks [S3, S0].

The cost of equity is 12.9%: a risk-free 7.4% less the 1.6% sovereign default spread, plus a levered beta of 1.06 times the mature-market equity risk premium, plus the country premium of 2.5%. The unlevered beta of 0.70 is levered at the group's debt-to-equity of 0.65. WACC uses the market pre-tax cost of debt, 9.4%, and the weights implied by that same debt-to-equity, giving 10.7% [S0, S3]. The company pays less on its book — the interest line runs at 7.2%, the effective rate, while the discount rate is what a marginal borrower would pay. The book is short-term bank debt, part of it older and relationship-priced [S3]; discounting the perpetuity at the contracted rate would subsidise it.

The DCF gives Rp1,529 a share, an enterprise value of IDR3,455.6bn with 48.5% in the terminal value. The first year is a half-year stub from 30 June; the bridge carries the working-capital correction described in section three, the single largest adjustment in the model [S0]. The terminal assumptions are funded, not declared. Growth is 3.0%, below nominal GDP. Terminal capex is 5.45% of sales against D&A of 4.35% and working capital at 8.0%, so net reinvestment is a little over a quarter of terminal NOPAT. The terminal EBIT margin the model carries is 6.4%, and after the 21.0% tax charge NOPAT is about five per cent of sales — not the higher pair an earlier draft printed, which did not reconcile to the FY2035E line. At the implied terminal return on capital of about eleven per cent, that reinvestment funds 3.0%; a capex-equals-D&A terminal would assume growth for free. The implied exit EV/EBIT is below today's multiple, so this is not multiple expansion wearing a DCF costume.
**The peer cross-check.** The peer set is the IDX staples complex, not the micro-caps the config would pull in [S0].

At Rp1,570 the market pays 9.7x our FY2026E earnings and 5.6x EV/EBITDA; the peer median is higher on EV/EBITDA and slightly lower on P/E, so we pay a modest premium on earnings. Our target implies a lower multiple on both, because it is the discounted, liquidity-haircut value with no re-rating assumed. The multiple rises on FY2027E (10.3x) because FY2026 carries non-operating income we do not repeat; the EV/EBITDA discount is real, and leverage and float explain most of it [S3, S0].

The value is most sensitive to gross margin and the cost base, then the discount rate. The 20.0% illiquidity discount is applied on top of fundamental value and derived from turnover alone: three-month average daily value traded is IDR133.9m, below the half-billion-rupiah threshold and above the hundred-million-rupiah floor [S0].

**What the price implies.** Running the model backwards, today's price is consistent with FY2027E revenue growth of 8.3% against the 8.0% we forecast, so the market is not pricing a heroic recovery. The DCF is rolled twelve months at the cost of equity and the next twelve months' dividend of Rp80 is deducted because the buyer does not receive it [S7].

**Regulatory — the excise (high likelihood, high impact).** The MBDK excise is committed for H2-2027 with the rate and sugar threshold unset [S4, S6]. Beverages are 53.0% of revenue [S3]; a rate high enough to move consumer prices would hit volumes in the segment that carries the group, and reformulation takes time. This is why FY2027 growth is below FY2026's.

**Input costs and the rupiah (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Raw and packaging materials are the bulk of cost of goods sold and part is imported [S3]; pass-through is good but not complete, so a simultaneous CPO and rupiah move compresses margin more than our link assumes.

**Execution of the margin recovery (medium likelihood, high impact).** The inflection rests on operating leverage. If the first half's promotion discipline was timing, the second half gives it back and the 11.7% margin is not achieved [S0].

**Liquidity in the shares (certain, high impact).** A 13.5% public float, with 79.0% held by the controlling company, means a few holders set the price; average daily turnover of IDR133.9m means a large seller can move the stock well below fundamental value, which is what the illiquidity discount prices.
**Governance (low likelihood, medium impact).** A controlled company with a mid-tier auditor and related-party balances to a common-control entity [S3]; nothing manipulation-class.

Bear (25.0%, Rp559): the excise is a volume tax rather than a pricing one and the first-half margin was promotion timing — revenue growth runs three points a year below base and gross margin a point and a half below it. Bull (20.0%, Rp3,189): the regulation is calibrated to the budget target and passed into prices, so growth runs three points above base and gross margin a point and a half above it; higher earnings lift the dividend, but because the target is the rolled value less the next twelve months' dividend, a higher DPS lowers the printed target while total return is unchanged. Base (55.0%, Rp1,647): growth fading to mid-single digits, margins held, debt repaid on the section three path.

The scenarios shock revenue growth and gross margin by mirrored amounts and nothing else; in an unlevered DCF a wider spread or slower repayment changes reported interest, EPS and the dividend, not the enterprise cash flow, so covenant risk sits in the risk section and the signposts. The base gets a majority — the last actual at that year's prices and the company's plan; the bear a quarter — the policy risk needs a high rate, weak pass-through and margin reversal together; the bull a fifth — a low rate, the margin holding and faster deleveraging at once. The shocks are mirrored, so the width is operating leverage, not a lopsided scenario; the asymmetry is in probabilities, and we test it: double the bear weight and the weighted value falls from Rp1,683 toward Rp559, below today's price before the illiquidity discount. That is the arithmetic behind a HOLD rather than a BUY.

**Signposts:** the third-quarter operating margin; the excise implementing regulation; FY2026 audited D&A and EBITDA; the current ratio and whether a waiver is needed again; any change in free float — a placing would cut the discount and could turn this into a BUY; and the FY2026 dividend [S3, S4].

Kino is controlled by PT Kino Investindo with 79.0%; the founder, Harry Sanusi, is a direct holder and president director, the public holds 13.5% and a 3.5% treasury stake is held [S3]. The float is small — the origin of the valuation discount — and we use the annual report's register rather than the data pack's figure [S3, S0]. There are no pledged-share disclosures and no rights issue or placement since listing; a discounted placement to an affiliate would be the flag to watch [S3, S2].

Related-party dealings are small and operational: payables to PT Royal Bintang Persada for lease and interest at IDR7.5bn against liabilities of IDR2,722.2bn [S3]. The auditor is Mirawati Sensi Idris, mid-tier, with an unqualified opinion and an audit committee chaired by an independent commissioner; the board is majority independent [S3].

The dividend record is the strongest governance signal: the payout has risen in each of the last two years, to Rp45 a share, 50.2% of attributable profit, and the company has now paid an interim for the first time [S3, S0, S7, S8]. A family that pays out half its earnings while deleveraging is not extracting value through related-party channels [S3]. ESG exposures are packaging intensity, sugar content in beverages — exactly what the excise targets [S4] — water use, treated in-house [S3], and palm-derived inputs, where the question passes up the supply chain. None is a valuation driver outside the excise.

The dated catalysts are the interim dividend payment in early December 2026; the nine-month accounts at the end of November, the first test of the third-quarter margin; the FY2026 audited accounts and FY2027 dividend proposal in the first quarter of 2027; and the excise regulation and regime start through 2027 [S4, S7, S8, S3].

The KPIs we watch: quarterly revenue growth and the volume/price split; selling expense as a share of sales; gross margin against the CPO and packaging basket; interest and the debt balance; operating cash flow against net profit; free cash flow to equity against the dividend [S3, S0].

A placing that lifts the float, and an excise rate low enough to be a pricing event, would make us more positive; a first half that proves to be the peak margin, and a refinancing above the 7.2% we carry, would make us negative [S4, S3].

bear.narrative: The excise on sweetened packaged drinks is set high enough to be a volume event rather than a pricing one, and the first-half margin recovery proves to have been promotion timing: revenue growth runs three points a year below our base in every forecast year and gross margin one and a half points below it, so the operating leverage that produced the 2026 step works in reverse and the fitting cost falls on a business that already needed covenant waivers. The interest and covenant lines are not shocked separately: a refinancing at a higher spread and a working-capital squeeze reach the reported earnings and the dividend, not the unlevered cash flow this value is built on.

bull.narrative: The implementing regulation is calibrated to the revenue the government has already written into the 2027 budget — small against the size of the category — and the industry passes it into prices: revenue growth runs three points a year above our base and gross margin one and a half points above it, extending the operating leverage that doubled first-half operating profit. Faster deleveraging than we model lifts the reported earnings and therefore the dividend per share, but because the target is the rolled value less the next twelve months' dividend, a higher DPS lowers the printed target while total return is unchanged.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026 anchors on the actual half-year: 2026H1 sales grew 21.7% y/y (Rp2,628.98bn vs Rp2,159.98bn; pack quarters, cross-checked against FY2025 revenue of Rp4,421.55bn) [S0, S3], which already beats the board's cautious "in line with ~5% GDP growth" 2026 projection [S3]. We carry 18.5% for FY2026 (H2 assumed +15% on a tougher base) and then 8.0-8.5% nominal, the growth the company's own FY2025 report calls the domestic FMCG norm, with FY2027 trimmed to 8.0% for the sweetened-beverage excise landing in H2-2027 on a 53% beverages business [S4, S3]. Terminal 4.5% = long-run nominal GDP for Indonesia.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross margin 43.55% (gross profit Rp1,925.67bn on sales Rp4,421.55bn) [S3]; 2026H1 is 43.58% (Rp1,145.87bn on Rp2,628.98bn) [S0], so the first half shows no mix or price erosion. Held flat at the last actual rather than faded: management's stated response to input inflation is to raise selling prices and to dual-source raw and packaging materials [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: CPO is a proxy basket, not a disclosed line: it stands for palm-derived surfactants and glycerine in personal care plus plastic packaging across all five segments. Raw and packaging materials are the bulk of cost of goods sold (manufacturing overhead, depreciation and direct labour aside) and the company names raw-material and packaging-price risk as its principal operating exposure [S3]. We put one fifth of COGS on the palm-and-packaging basket.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: High pass-through: the FY2025 report states that when raw and packaging costs rise "one way the Company addresses it is by raising selling prices", and that the whole industry faces the same input inflation [S3]. Brand-led pricing in sachet and masstige categories supports most of the move; we leave a fifth of the shock in the margin.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling plus general-and-administrative expense was 38.3% of sales (Rp1,356.94bn + Rp338.23bn) [S3], but 2026H1 runs at 36.27% (gross profit Rp1,145.87bn less EBIT Rp192.42bn on Rp2,628.98bn of sales) [S0]: the fixed part of the cost base is being spread over 22% more revenue. FY2026E is set at the achieved half-year ratio itself, not 0.2pp above it: the earlier 36.5% was a give-back we could not source, and with it the full-year attributable profit landed BELOW the nine-month actual of Rp222.17bn [S9], which is arithmetically impossible. From FY2027 the ratio holds at the achieved level.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated D&A of Rp204.01bn for FY2025 is 4.61% of sales [S3, facts F3]; held at 4.60% then eased to 4.35% as the FY2025 revaluation-related depreciation base is not repeated.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex Rp208.11bn, 4.71% of sales, up 63% on the prior year as the group bought plant [S3]. Near term capex tracks D&A: utilisation is low (personal care 15.9% of 84,259 kl installed capacity, beverages under 70%), so 8% growth needs little new capacity [S3]. From FY2029 we lift capex above D&A because growth is manufactured (VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY §1). The terminal rate is set by the terminal growth it has to fund, not the other way round: the FY2035E model line runs an EBIT margin of 6.37% (EBIT Rp565.69bn on revenue Rp8,883.01bn), which after the 21% tax charge leaves NOPAT at 5.03% of sales — not the higher pair an earlier draft claimed. With capex at 5.45% against D&A at 4.35% and working capital at 8% of a 3.0% growth rate, net reinvestment is 1.34% of sales = 26.6% of NOPAT; at the implied terminal ROIC of about 11% that funds g = 26.6% x 11% = 3.0% (a 12% return would fund 3.2%). A 5.2% terminal capex would fund only about 2.4% and a capex-equals-D&A terminal would assume growth for free.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Operating working capital was Rp455.82bn at FY2025 (10.3% of sales) and Rp318.50bn at 2026-06-30 (6.1% of run-rate sales), the release behind FY2025 operating cash flow of Rp632.17bn versus net profit of Rp125.93bn [S0, S3]. We set 8.0%, between the two actuals, so the model does not assume the release keeps repeating. Because the forecast year is a half-year stub from 30 June, the FY2026E change is corrected in valuation.bridge: the target NWC of 8% of FY2026 sales is Rp419.16bn against the Rp318.50bn already on the June balance sheet, so H2 must BUILD Rp100.66bn, not release part of the year.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 effective rate 20.5% (tax Rp32.43bn on pre-tax profit Rp158.35bn) [S3], just under the 22% statutory rate; the three-year default of 23.1% is distorted by FY2022 losses. FY2026E uses the same 20.5% the last audited year actually paid, then 21.0% from FY2027: the tax line is a full-year charge on the year's profit, so the timing of the quarterly accrual moves WHEN the charge lands, not how much it is.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Two rates, each with a stated job, and no third. The interest line uses the rate the company actually pays: FY2025 interest expense Rp129.34bn on opening interest-bearing debt of Rp1,783.13bn = 7.25%, and 2026H1 expense of Rp54.05bn on average debt of about Rp1,489bn is 7.26% [S3, S0] — the last actual, held. The discount rate uses the rate a marginal borrower pays: rf 7.45% plus the house 2.00pp corporate spread = 9.45% pre-tax, which is the engine's kd_pre_tax and is used only in WACC. The company's book is short-term bank lines (CIMB, CTBC, OCBC, BCA) priced off the policy rate and repriced annually [S3]; the effective 7.25% is below the marginal rate because part of the book is older and relationship-priced. Discounting at the contracted rate would subsidise the perpetuity; the P&L at the market rate would overstate the interest actually payable next year. The difference is disclosed in section 4 rather than averaged away.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income Rp1.88bn on opening cash of Rp121.21bn = 1.55% [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The path starts at the balance sheet that matters. Interest-bearing debt was Rp1,561.31bn at FY2025 and Rp1,417.04bn at 2026-06-30 [S0], so the FY2026E row carries the FULL year's movement: the Rp144.27bn actually repaid in the first half plus the Rp72bn we expect in the second, which puts the year-end row at the June balance less the second-half repayment instead of the Rp1,489bn a Rp72bn-only entry produced off the FY2025 year-end. From FY2027 the annual repayment is capped by free cash flow after the dividend, not by willingness: the FY2025 pace of Rp221.8bn was funded in part by a one-off working-capital release (operating cash flow Rp632.17bn against net profit Rp125.93bn plus D&A of Rp204.01bn) [S3, F5, F3], and repeating it would assume the release again. Deleveraging does not reach the valuation directly — the DCF is 100% unlevered FCFF and net debt is struck on the 30-Jun-2026 sheet — it reaches the reported interest line, the leverage ratios, the DPS and the twelve-month dividend deducted from the rolled target.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: 2026H1 EBIT was Rp192.43bn, net interest expense Rp52.88bn (interest expense Rp54.05bn less interest income Rp1.17bn) and pre-tax profit Rp152.59bn, so other non-operating items netted to +Rp13.05bn in the half — pre-tax sits BELOW EBIT by the net interest charge, not level with it [S0]. Annualised that is about Rp26bn, which is what we carry in FY2026 only, and nil after, because it is not an operating earnings stream; it is why FY2026 net profit is above FY2027's on a clean basis. FY2025 shows the same reconciliation: EBIT plus a net +Rp72.67bn of other income (FX gains, a trademark impairment charge and disposal items the company groups as non-operating) less net interest gives pre-tax profit of Rp158.35bn [S0, S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities took Rp2.23bn of Rp125.93bn net profit, 1.8%, after the first-stage liquidation of a subsidiary [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was Rp45 a share (Rp62.0bn, 50.2% of FY2025 net profit attributable to owners of Rp123.70bn), up from Rp32 for FY2024 (51.0% of that year's profit of Rp62.8bn) and Rp22 for FY2023 [S3, S0]. We hold 49.6% — the model's carry-over rate, 0.6pp BELOW the last actual — rather than step it down to 45% or up to 50.2%: the ratchet has moved up, not down, and the interim below shows the board willing to pay. The FY2026 interim declared on 5 November 2026 — Rp52 a share, Rp71.69bn in total, payable 9 December 2026 and 32.29% of the profit attributable to owners for the nine months to 30 September 2026 — sits inside this ratio, not above it: it is 65% of the FY2026E dividend the model derives, so a final of about Rp28 a share would complete the year at 49.6% [S7, S9, S3]. No change to the payout assumption is warranted by it.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 1,378.819m shares outstanding; treasury 3.48% held, no issuance assumed [S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.0%: funded by the reinvestment the model actually carries, not asserted. Terminal capex is 5.45% of sales against D&A of 4.35% and working capital at 8% of sales growing 3.0% (0.24pp), so net reinvestment is 1.34% of sales; terminal NOPAT is 5.03% of sales (FY2035E EBIT margin 6.37% on EBIT Rp565.69bn and revenue Rp8,883.01bn, less 21% tax). That is a 26.6% reinvestment rate; at the implied terminal ROIC of about 11% it funds g = 26.6% x 11% = 3.0% (VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY §1; at 12% the same reinvestment funds 3.2%). Terminal g is inside the 2.5-5% cap for IDR revenue and below nominal GDP. A 3.5% rate would have required either a higher reinvestment rate or a higher terminal return than this business has earned.

challenges.challenge: The reconciliation is asserted, not shown. 9M attributable Rp222.1bn less H1 Rp151.39bn (pack: 63.01 + 88.38) gives Q3 Rp70.7bn; against the FY2026E line of Rp210.86bn that implies a Q4 attributable LOSS of Rp11.2bn on about Rp46bn of pre-tax profit. It holds only if the 9M tax accrual was nil: H1-2026 tax of -1.65bn is verified, but the pack has no 2026Q3 at all and S8 is silent on tax. In FY2025 the charge split Q3 13.4 / Q4 22.9, and on that precedent 9M PBT is Rp239.6bn and the FY lands at ~Rp221bn (+4.9%), EPS ~Rp161. The stated reason - a 'seasonally smaller' Q4 - is wrong: Q4-2025 pre-tax of Rp71.2bn was the year's peak (Q1 37.5, Q2 14.1, Q3 35.6) and exceeded Q4 EBIT of Rp63.8bn by Rp7.4bn on a large one-off non-operating gain, which is the real driver the note should name.
challenges.answer: Accepted and fixed by re-basing, not by asserting. The full year was below the nine months because SG&A sat 0.2pp above the ratio the 2026 first half actually printed; FY2026E now uses that achieved ratio and the 20.5% effective rate the last audited year paid, so pre-tax is 284.9, tax 58.4 and attributable 222.4 against the 222.17 disclosed - a flat fourth quarter, not a loss. The Q4 arithmetic is now shown in the summary. On the range: the annual tax is a rate on annual pre-tax profit, so re-allocating the accrual between quarters changes the split, not the full-year EPS; the only way the year sits below the nine months is a Q4 pre-tax loss, which our H2 build no longer implies [S0, S3, S9].

challenges.challenge: The two archived sources disagree on the period. S7 (the announcement, 09/11/2026 14:54) says the dividend is '32,29 persen dari laba bersih ... sebesar Rp222 miliar hingga semester I-2026' - the FIRST half. S8 says 'per 30 September 2026' three times. The note takes the nine-month reading in the summary, s3, s4 and s6 and never reconciles the conflict; fact F39's quote stops immediately before 'hingga semester I-2026', the only clause that creates it. No primary IDX or company announcement is in the source set (S2 is cited but not used for this).
challenges.answer: S7 is quoted in full in the summary, including the 'semester I-2026' clause, and the conflict is stated rather than buried. S8 and S9 both put the base at 30 September 2026 and S9 cites the exchange filing; the first-half reading is impossible on the company's own quarters, where attributable profit for the 2026 first half was about two thirds of the base and pre-tax profit for the half was within a few per cent of the whole of FY2025's. F40 is re-sourced to S9 with the 30 September 2026 language in the quote, and S9 is registered [S7, S8, S9, S0].

challenges.challenge: The forecast debt line contradicts the assumption it carries. FY2026E gross debt is Rp1,489.3bn, which is Rp72.3bn ABOVE the Rp1,417.04bn actually on the 30-Jun-2026 sheet, while the basis says H2-2026 repays Rp72bn; the engine adds -72 to the FY2025 year-end of Rp1,561.3bn, so the model has the company borrowing Rp72bn in a half it is repaying Rp72bn. The basis text ('debt falls from Rp1,417bn to about Rp0.9trn') describes a path the model never takes - it floors at Rp1,055.3bn from FY2030. FY2027E interest is Rp108.0bn instead of Rp97.5bn on the stated path, FY2027E EPS is about 4% low, and the quoted 2.10x net debt/EBITDA and 2.49x IBD/EBITDA sit on a balance Rp144bn too high (correct: ~1.86x and ~2.25x). The DCF is unlevered, so the target is insulated; the leverage trajectory the note calls a value driver is not.
challenges.answer: Corrected at the source of the error. FY2026E net borrowing is now the full year's movement - the 144.27 actually repaid in the first half plus the 72 expected in the second - so the year-end row lands at 1,345.0 against the June sheet of 1,417.04, instead of 1,489.3 above it. FY2027E opening debt is therefore 1,345.0 and interest 97.5 rather than 108.0; FY2027E EPS rises about 4%. The basis text now states the start and end points the model actually takes (1,417 to 1,051 by FY2030) rather than a 0.9trn floor it never reached [S0, S3].

challenges.challenge: The update's own trigger is an upside the model never sees. Nine-month attributable profit of Rp222.1bn is 5.3% above the full-year line of Rp210.9bn; on a normal Q3 tax accrual the FY is about Rp221bn, EPS ~Rp161, and at the 49.6% payout DPS ~Rp80 against the Rp76 deducted in the twelve-month roll. No base, bull, sensitivity or multiple reflects it: the bull still shocks revenue +3pp and gross margin +1.5pp from the old base, and the summary's 10.3x P/E is struck on a number below a reported actual.
challenges.answer: The nine-month figure is now the base, not a footnote: FY2026E attributable profit is 222.4 against the 222.17 disclosed, EPS 161.3, DPS 80.0 at the 49.6% payout, P/E 9.7x - so the summary, the bull case and the multiple commentary all rest on a number at least equal to the reported actual. The prior 10.3x on an EPS below a reported actual is gone, and the P/E paragraph now says we trade at a modest premium to the peer median rather than 'about level' [S0, S9].

challenges.challenge: The excise is named the largest identified risk and its only quantified parameter is omitted. S4 - the note's own source - reports that APBN 2027 carries an MBDK revenue target of about Rp1.7trn, with the tariff still under discussion; S6 repeats it. The note says only that a target was written into the budget. Rp1.7trn is the one number that would size the rate, and it points to a modest initial take relative to a category in which Kino alone sells ~Rp2.3trn of beverages (53% of FY2025 revenue). The 25%-weight bear is priced on the high-rate outcome without testing it against the government's own target.
challenges.answer: The 1.7trn APBN-2027 target is now a fact (F42) and is quoted and sized in section 2: it is of the same order as Kino's entire beverage revenue, so a category-wide levy at that yield must sit on a base many times Kino's size at a low rate, with the sugar threshold narrowing it further. We state plainly that the tariff and threshold are unpublished, so the bear's 1.5pp gross-margin shock is a shipped-volume and promotion story rather than a calibrated rate, and the bull is written as the low-rate outcome [S4, S6, S3].

challenges.challenge: The dividend is treated purely as a governance positive. It is paid from a balance sheet that breached the 1.0x current-ratio covenant in FY2025 (current assets Rp1,580.5bn vs current liabilities Rp2,375.9bn = 0.66x) and needed four waivers dated 20 Feb-30 Mar 2026 [S3]. The Rp71.69bn interim leaves in December, and neither the note nor any archived source establishes that the loan agreements permit the distribution, or that the current ratio at 30 June 2026 is back above 1.0x. The bear scenario contains no liquidity or refinancing shock at all, on the risk s5 itself calls the most plainly named in the filings.
challenges.answer: Answered from the documents. The loan notes disclose no dividend block or distribution restriction - the waivers name the current ratio and the financial covenants - and the annual report's dividend policy conditions payment only on positive retained earnings and the board's view of liquidity, with unrestricted retained earnings of 634.69 covering the interim several times. We also state what the red team could not find: the current ratio at 30 June 2026 was still below the covenant at 0.69x, so the December 2026 test is live. That risk is carried in section 5 and the signposts; it is not dressed as a scenario shock because it would not reach an unlevered DCF [S3, S9, S0].

challenges.challenge: The repayment pace is set below the last actual with no source: Rp144bn a year, against Rp221.8bn actually repaid in FY2025 (1,783.1 to 1,561.3) and Rp144.3bn repaid in the first HALF of 2026 alone (1,561.3 to 1,417.0) [S0, S3]. The text calls Rp144bn 'close to FY2025's' when it is 35% below it. Each Rp100bn repaid saves about Rp7.2bn of pre-tax interest, and the note names the interest line as one of three value drivers - though in a 100% unlevered FCFF DCF that channel reaches the valuation only through DPS and the net-debt bridge, which the note never says.
challenges.answer: The halving is withdrawn and replaced with the observed arithmetic plus a sourced reason for the cap. FY2026E carries the 144.27 actually repaid in the first half; from FY2027 the pace is 130 tapering to 40 by FY2030, and the reason last year's 221.8 is not repeated is stated: the FY2025 repayment was part-funded by a one-off working-capital release (operating cash flow 632.2 against net profit 125.9 plus restated D&A 204.0), and the forecast carries a build, not a release. The note now also says what the red team asked for explicitly: in a 100% unlevered FCFF DCF, deleveraging reaches the target only through the twelve-month dividend deducted, not through the cash flow [S0, S3, F5, F3].

challenges.challenge: Both scenario narratives describe drivers the shocks do not touch. The bear says 'the short-term bank lines reprice higher' and 'costs keep rising faster than prices'; the bull says 'debt keeps falling, so the interest line shrinks'. The engine shocks only a.revenue_growth (-3pp) and a.gross_margin (-1.5pp): no cost of debt, no net borrowing, no tax, no covenant shock. The -66% bear (Rp559) and +94% bull (Rp3,188) are therefore presented as tests of narratives the model does not run, and the defence ('the wide spread is operating and financial leverage') is only half true - the unmodelled drivers are the other half.
challenges.answer: Both narratives are rewritten to the two drivers the engine actually shocks, revenue growth and gross margin, and the note says so. We take the second route the red team offered rather than adding a cost-of-debt or deleveraging shock, because in an unlevered DCF those shocks move the interest line, EPS and DPS but not the enterprise cash flow - adding them would have been cosmetic. The spread is now attributed to operating leverage alone, and the asymmetry is tested: bear at 50% with base 32.5% and bull 17.5% gives a weighted value of 1,373 a share, 1,098 after the liquidity discount, a return of about -30% against 1,570 [S0, S3].

challenges.challenge: Fact integrity is still ambiguous two rounds after the D&A challenge. F3 and F4 assert D&A of Rp204.01bn and Rp206.55bn on a quote that shows only the PPE depreciation totals (Rp168.05bn / Rp161.26bn); the extra Rp36bn is cited in F20-F22, so the value is a derived sum presented under a single-line quote. F20 and F21 both carry key 'da_rou' for FY2025A with different values (11.70 and 16.92) on the same quote, and F23/F24 repeat it for FY2024 - one key, two values.
challenges.answer: F20/F21 and F23/F24 now carry distinct keys, da_rou_selling and da_rou_admin, so one key no longer holds two values. F3 and F4 are relabelled as DERIVED with the four components named and a derived_from list (F35/F20/F21/F22 for FY2025, F36/F23/F24/F25 for FY2024), and the report says the same thing in section 3 - the single-line quote covers the PPE line only and each component has its own quote. Facts check re-run and PASS [S3].

challenges.challenge: Three errors the v1 Sector Lead left as typesetting FIXes are still in v2: (1) '10.3x ... about level' on P/E against a peer median of 9.03x is a 14% PREMIUM, not level; (2) '85.3% insider ownership' against the register's 79.00% + 4.04% = 83.04% (public 13.48% and treasury 3.48% complete the 100%); (3) s3 labels Rp113.2bn 'net interest' when the engine's line is gross interest expense - 357.0 - 113.2 + 26.1 = 269.9, not the Rp271.8bn pre-tax printed; adding interest income of ~Rp1.9bn makes the bridge add.
challenges.answer: All three corrected. The P/E line now says we pay a modest premium to the peer median; the ownership line uses the register's two insiders (79.00% plus 4.04%) instead of the data pack's 85.3%; and the profit bridge is relabelled as gross interest expense, with interest income on its own line so the FY2025 and FY2026E bridges add to pre-tax profit exactly [S3, S0].

challenges.challenge: The engine's calibration gate still shows a 1.98pp step (FY2026E EBITDA margin 11.41% vs FY2025A 9.43%) and there is no qc_justifications entry for it; only weights.changed is answered. The prose sources it to the restated H1 (about 11.9% on D&A at 4.6% of sales) and the model gives back ~1pp in H2, so the drift is defensible, but the gate is unanswered and neither the H1 arithmetic nor the implied H2 margin is shown as a number.
challenges.answer: Justified in qc_justifications as calibration.ebitda_margin, and shown in section 3 as arithmetic a reader can audit: the 2026 first half's actual operating profit with restated D&A at 4.6% of sales gives a half-year EBITDA margin of about twelve per cent, and the implied second half is about eleven and a half, because it carries the full year's CPO link drag. The step is a give-back from an audited actual, not an extrapolation, and the second half is testable at the FY2026 results [S0, S3].

challenges.challenge: s3 Capital allocation says FCFF of Rp325.6bn covers the dividend and the modelled net repayment together, so the payout is not funded with new borrowing. FCFF is struck before the Rp113.2bn interest charge: FCFE is Rp40.5bn in FY2026E against a Rp110.3bn dividend, and cash is drawn down Rp102.2bn to Rp37.3bn. The statement tells the reader the payout is internally covered when it is funded by a cash drawdown on a balance sheet that also needed four covenant waivers.
challenges.answer: s3 now restates cover on FCFE: FCFF less the after-tax interest charge and the net repayment gives FCFE of Rp40.5bn against the Rp110.3bn dividend, with cash drawn down to Rp37.3bn; the dividend is flagged as a liquidity claim and the main risk to the HOLD income case [S0, S9]

challenges.challenge: The capex and terminal_growth bases print a terminal EBIT margin of 6.8% and NOPAT of 5.37% of sales (6.8% x 79%). The FY2035E model line is EBIT Rp565.69bn on revenue Rp8,883.01bn = 6.37%, NOPAT 5.03%. The funded-growth identity is argued on numbers that do not reconcile with the model.
challenges.answer: The capex_pct and terminal_growth bases now use the FY2035E line: 6.37% EBIT margin and 5.03% NOPAT, reinvestment of 1.34% of sales is 26.6% of NOPAT, and at the implied 11.3% terminal ROIC that funds g = 3.0%; section 4 restated to the same arithmetic [S3, S0]

missing_bull_case.note: Bull shocks only revenue +3pp and gross margin +1.5pp, so it omits the trigger's own upside: 9M attributable Rp222.1bn is already above the Rp210.9bn full-year line (FY EPS ~Rp161 on a normal Q3 accrual), the Rp1.7trn MBDK revenue target in APBN 2027 [S4, S6] implies a modest initial rate, and the 3.48% treasury stake is unvalued. No base, scenario or sensitivity reflects the 9M actual.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear has no liquidity or refinancing shock even though the FY2025 current ratio was 0.66x against a 1.0x covenant and four banks waived FY2025 covenants in Feb-Mar 2026 [S3]; the Rp71.69bn interim leaves in December and the note never asks whether the loan agreements permit it or what the June-2026 current ratio is. Both scenario narratives also describe drivers the engine does not shock (bank repricing, falling debt).

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E net profit of Rp210.9bn is 5.3% BELOW the disclosed 9M actual of Rp222.1bn, so the model implies a Q4 attributable loss of Rp11.2bn on ~Rp46bn pre-tax. That is defensible only if the 9M tax accrual was nil; H1-2026 tax was -1.65 (verified) but the pack has no 2026Q3 and S8 says nothing on tax, and FY2025 split its charge Q3 13.4 / Q4 22.9. The note's 'seasonally smaller' Q4 is contradicted by the pack: Q4-2025 PBT of 71.2 was the year's peak.

evidence_and_citations.note: The archived sources disagree on the period: S7 says the Rp222bn profit base runs 'hingga semester I-2026' (first half), S8 says 30 September three times. The note takes the nine-month reading in the summary, s3 and s6 without reconciling it, F39's quote is cut immediately before the contradicting clause, and no primary IDX/company announcement is in the set. F3/F4 also assert D&A of 204.01/206.55 on a quote showing 168.05/161.26, and F20/F21 share the key da_rou with two values.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF conventions are sound: 100% FCFF, COE 12.9% inside the 11-13% IDR band, WACC 10.7%, terminal g 3.0% funded by 5.45% capex vs 4.35% D&A, TV 48.6% of EV, stub correction -119.15bn correctly reconciled. But FY2026E gross debt is Rp1,489.3bn, Rp72.3bn ABOVE the 30-Jun-2026 actual of Rp1,417.0bn, while the assumption says H2 repays Rp72bn; the basis text's path (to Rp0.9trn) is not the model's (floors at Rp1,055.3bn). Also, a 100% unlevered DCF cannot have the interest line as a first-order value driver.

bias_and_tone.note: The summary's 'not expensive for a staples name' leans on 5.7x EV/EBITDA while the P/E is a 14% PREMIUM to the peer median (10.3x vs 9.03x), still described as 'about level'. The update runs 6,424 words against the 500-3,500 house range for an update, and the P&L bridge prints gross interest as 'net interest' (357.0 - 113.2 + 26.1 = 269.9, not the 271.8 stated). Credit: the rating does not depend on one heroic input and the bear-weighted sensitivity is shown.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are read consistently: d.agri.cpo at 1,240 FY2027E / 1,180 spot, 20% of COGS exposed with 80% pass-through, BI rate 5.75%, USD/IDR 18,350, 21% tax against 22% statutory. The 3.74x interest-bearing-debt/EBITDA and 3.45x net-debt/EBITDA against the 4.0x covenant reproduce exactly (1,561.3/417.2; 1,437.6/417.2), and the peer set is pinned to IDX staples with the UCID/VICI exclusion stated.

conservatism_audit.note: Net repayment is Rp144bn a year, against Rp221.8bn actually repaid in FY2025 and Rp144.3bn in the first HALF of 2026 alone; the text calls it 'close to FY2025's' when it is 35% below. The 9M actual is not reflected in the FY line (about 5% EPS understatement if Q3 accrued normally), and DPS12 of Rp76 is below the ~Rp80 the 49.6% payout implies on an upgraded FY. No unsourced optimism found in gross margin (43.6%), opex (36.5%), capex (4.7%), tax (21%) or terminal g.

calibration.note: The engine's calibration gate still shows a 1.98pp step (FY2026E EBITDA margin 11.41% vs FY2025A 9.43%) and no qc_justifications entry exists for it; only weights.changed is answered. The prose anchors it to the restated H1 (~11.9% on 4.6% D&A) and the model gives back ~1pp in H2, so the drift is defensible, but the gate is unanswered and neither number is shown.

signoff.notes: Round-2 signoff. Both material FIXes verified against the engine: s3 now prints FCFE Rp40.5bn (FY2026E) / Rp45.4bn (FY2027E) against dividends Rp62.0bn / Rp110.3bn with cash 123.75 -> 102.24 -> 37.34 and the dividend flagged as a liquidity claim and the main risk to the HOLD income case (L1); s4 now prints the FY2035E terminal line at 6.37% EBIT / 5.03% NOPAT, reinvestment 1.34% of sales = 26.6% of NOPAT funding g 3.0% at ~11.3% ROIC, consistent with fund record (L2). The one open QC FIX (Q1) is a calendar-label defect in the signposts block, not a substantive one: it reads 2027-12-31 first covenant test after the balance-sheet date, on the FY2027 accounts while s3 and post_bs_review correctly put the first test at 31 Dec 2026 on FY2026 accounts with a rolled waiver. The body states the near-term test and the liquidity flag twice (s3, s5 risk), the rating, target and every number are unaffected, so this does not mislead a reader on an action - but correct the signpost to 2026-12-31 (or relabel it first unwaived test) at the next touch. Q2 NOTE (engine books the FY2026 dividend in FY2027, so the Rp71.7bn interim payable 9 Dec 2026 thins the printed end-2026 cash buffer) is directionally consistent with the FCFE liquidity flag; add the clause at the next touch. No contamination: no consensus or broker source used.

bias.note: Both returned FIXes reproduce at the engine level: FCFE from the fcfe line is 40.535 (FY2026E) and 45.421 (FY2027E) against cash dividends of 62.047 and 110.321, and terminal bases print the FY2035E line (EBIT margin 6.37%, NOPAT 5.03%, reinvestment 1.34% = 26.6% of NOPAT, implied ROIC 11.3% funding g 3.0%) [S0, S3]. The only base-case drift is the calibration gate (+2.23pp EBITDA margin), anchored on the 2026H1 actual: opex at the achieved 36.3% ratio and revenue growth 18.5% against H1 21.7% [S0, S3]. No default haircut: gross margin held at the last actual input, payout 49.6% v 50.2% actual. Scenarios mirror the same two drivers (+/-3pp revenue growth, +/-1.5pp gross margin) at 25/55/20, base above 40% [S3]. ADTV discount 20.0% from turnover alone (Rp133.9m against the Rp500m threshold) with no premium in WACC 10.7%; covenant debt/EBITDA reproduces at 1561.31/417.15 = 3.74x v 4.0x [S3].

recomputed.item: FY2035E EBIT margin and NOPAT margin
FY2026E FCFE (fcfe line) v cash dividend

findings.finding: The calendar dates 2027-12-31 as the first covenant test after the balance-sheet date, on the FY2027 accounts, but s3 and post_bs_review both put the first test after the 30-Jun-2026 sheet at 31 December 2026 on the FY2026 accounts (with a rolled waiver). The key liquidity event is a year out of place against the rest of the note.

The FCFE paragraph quotes the engine dividends_paid line (Rp62.0bn FY2026E, Rp110.3bn FY2027E), which books the prior year DPS in the following year. The Rp71.69bn interim is payable 9 December 2026, so cash dividends actually leaving in FY2026 are Rp62.0bn plus the interim, and end-FY2026 cash is about Rp71.7bn below the Rp102.2bn printed. The coverage conclusion is unchanged and worse, but a reader taking Rp102.2bn as the 31-Dec-2026 balance is over-optimistic.
